items.followUp: Name the two main stages of the cell cycle.

rubric.why: Interphase is one of the two major phases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming interphase correctly.

rubric.why: The mitotic phase is the other major phase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the mitotic phase or mitosis.

items.followUp: What happens to DNA during the S phase of interphase?

rubric.why: S stands for synthesis, identifying this stage of interphase.
rubric.description: Identifies S phase as the synthesis phase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that S phase is the synthesis phase.

rubric.why: DNA is copied during this phase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that DNA is replicated or copied.

modelAnswer: S phase is the synthesis phase of interphase.

rubric.why: Mitosis is the division of the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the nucleus divides.

rubric.why: Mitosis produces two daughter nuclei with the same genetic information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that two genetically identical daughter nuclei are produced, or that they retain the same chromosome number.

modelAnswer: Mitosis is the division of a cell’s nucleus into two genetically identical daughter nuclei.
The daughter nuclei have the same number of chromosomes as the parent nucleus.

items.followUp: Differentiate between aerobic respiration and anaerobic respiration.

rubric.why: Catabolism is the breakdown of complex molecules into simpler ones.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying breakdown of complex molecules into simpler substances.

rubric.why: Catabolic reactions release energy, whereas anabolic reactions use energy to build complex molecules.
rubric.description: Contrasts the energy changes in catabolism and anabolism.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly distinguishing energy release in catabolism from energy use in anabolism.

modelAnswer: Catabolism breaks complex molecules into simpler substances and releases energy.
Anabolism builds complex molecules from simpler substances and requires energy.

items.followUp: Write down two ways enzymes help living organisms.

rubric.why: Enzymes catalyse the breakdown of food during digestion.
rubric.description: Gives digestion as a use of enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes help digest or break down food.

rubric.why: Enzymes are used in practical applications and catalyse chemical reactions.
rubric.description: Gives another valid use of enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one other valid use, such as use in detergents, food processing, or medicine, or catalysis of chemical reactions.

modelAnswer: Enzymes help in the digestion of food.
Enzymes are used in detergents to remove stains.

items.followUp: What is meant by energy transformation in living organisms?

rubric.why: Bioenergetics concerns energy and its transformations.
rubric.description: Identifies energy as the subject of bioenergetics.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for referring to the study of energy or energy transformations.

rubric.why: Bioenergetics studies these processes in living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the study concerns living organisms.

modelAnswer: Bioenergetics is the study of energy transformations in living organisms.

items.followUp: Name the nitrogenous base and sugar present in ATP.

rubric.why: Adenine and ribose are components of ATP.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly naming adenine and ribose.
Award 1 mark for stating that ATP has three phosphate groups.

items.followUp: Write the balanced chemical equation for photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Carbon dioxide and water are the reactants in photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including carbon dioxide and water on the reactant side.
Award 1 mark for including glucose and oxygen on the product side.
